title: There’s a Place on Earth Where Lightning Strikes Almost Every Night
start_frame_prompt: Ultra-photorealistic vertical cinematic night aerial over Lake Maracaibo region Venezuela, dark tropical water, distant shoreline and mountain silhouettes, enormous convective thundercloud tower illuminated internally by lightning, humid atmospheric depth, documentary storm photography, realistic exposure, no text, no fantasy colors.
negative_prompt: cartoon, infographic, labels, purple fantasy lightning, city destruction, tornado, apocalypse, fake branching, repeated identical bolts, text, watermark, black bars
narration: Near Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, thunderstorms return with extraordinary frequency. The phenomenon is called Catatumbo lightning. Warm, moist air over the lake interacts with surrounding terrain and regional winds, helping powerful nighttime storms form again and again. Lightning activity can occur on many nights of the year, with intense flashes concentrated over the same region. It is not one permanent thunderstorm and not literally every single night. The remarkable part is how reliably the local geography and atmosphere rebuild the conditions for lightning.
captions: WARM MOIST AIR MEETS COMPLEX TERRAIN.
NIGHT STORMS RETURN AGAIN AND AGAIN.
NOT ONE ENDLESS STORM — A REPEATING SYSTEM.

scenes.prompt: Begin on the exact night aerial. A realistic lightning discharge illuminates the giant convective cloud and reflects softly on Lake Maracaibo. Drone camera advances toward the storm while preserving shoreline and mountain geography. Bolts vary naturally and originate within the cloud system; no repeated stock-like flash, no apocalypse, premium storm documentary realism.

Continue the same camera path and descend toward the lake surface before sunrise. Impossible weather-documentary time compression reveals warm humid air rising from the dark water as subtle physically realistic vapor and cloud development, while cooler regional airflow descends from surrounding terrain. Do not draw arrows or colored air streams; communicate airflow through cloud and mist motion.

Camera rises continuously with developing moist convection into a towering cumulonimbus. Show real cloud microphysics at cinematic scale: droplets, turbulent updraft texture and charge-separation conditions implied by ice and graupel collisions, without labels or glowing particles. Transition from exterior cloud to an impossible internal storm view while maintaining orientation and realistic darkness.

Inside-to-outside continuous camera move as charge separation culminates in a branching lightning channel forming through the cloud and connecting toward the lower atmosphere. The flash must obey natural lightning geometry and exposure, briefly revealing cloud structure and lake below. No slow floating electricity, no sci-fi energy beam, no repeated identical bolt.

Pull far back into a high night aerial over the same Lake Maracaibo geography. Use restrained time compression to show multiple separate storm cells developing and flashing across the region over time, emphasizing recurrence rather than one permanent storm. End on a spectacular but photoreal wide shot with mountains framing the basin; no generated text or fantasy grading.

production_notes.director_intent: Make geography itself the reveal: lake + mountains repeatedly rebuild the storm engine. Exterior storm spectacle transitions into hidden atmospheric mechanism and back to regional scale.
production_notes.science_guard: Do not claim lightning occurs literally every night or that a single storm is permanent. Describe exceptional annual frequency and regional atmospheric/topographic contribution without asserting one oversimplified cause as settled fact.
production_notes.sound_design: Natural narration; distant thunder with realistic delay and dynamics, water ambience in exterior shots, no constant thunder wall or synthetic zaps.
